Authority to assist friendly countries and international organizations with peacekeeping operations and other programs that serve U.S. national security interests. The account pays for missions outside UN assessed budgets and for building partners' capacity to deploy peacekeepers; U.S. assessed dues for UN peacekeeping come from a separate State Department account.

::: {.official-links}

[Enacted text: 92 Stat. 736](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/92/736){.btn-official} [Current U.S. Code: 22 U.S.C. 2348](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/22/2348?link-type=html){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- Sec. 551: assistance, on terms the President determines, for peacekeeping operations and other programs in furtherance of U.S. national security interests.
- May reimburse the Defense Department for support under Sec. 7 of the [UN Participation Act](unpa-1945.qmd), up to $5 million a year unless more is authorized.
- The annual appropriation sets amounts and adds conditions, including [Leahy Laws](leahy-laws.qmd) vetting and the [coup restriction](sec7008-coup.qmd).

## Why it matters

Peacekeeping Operations is the State Department's main tool for supporting regional missions and training foreign peacekeepers, which places it between foreign aid and security cooperation. It shows the Title 22 alternative to deploying U.S. forces: paying and equipping others to keep the peace, under foreign affairs committee oversight.

## Current status

In force. Funded each year in Title IV of the State-foreign operations appropriations act. Check current status.

[Last checked November 24, 2026.]{.checked}

## Funding and administration

- **Account.** Peacekeeping Operations, Title IV (International Security Assistance) in the [State-foreign ops appropriations](sfops-approps-annual.qmd).
- **Run by.** The State Department (Bureau of Political-Military Affairs).
- **Committees.** Authorizing, House Foreign Affairs and Senate Foreign Relations; appropriations, the House and Senate subcommittees for State and foreign operations.
